deepdive.sec: Eastern India Tertiary Care Hospitals & Surgical Platforms

bull_bear.body: Disciplined greenfield expansion in underserved Eastern/Central markets; 90% of Jamshedpur capex deployed in FY27; Evaluating M&A for 150-200 bed assets; No dividend commentary provided.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raipur ramp-up delay beyond Q3FY27 breakeven target; Insurance empanelment delays (critical for Raipur volume); Staff attrition due to new competitor entry in Raipur; Bangladesh geopolitical/visa volatility impacting Agartala volumes; West Bengal election aftermath impact on scheme patients (minimal expected).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on structural demand in Eastern India; Pragmatic on Raipur losses (temporary); Aggressive on specialty mix upgrades (robotics, transplants); Clear on 24-36 month breakeven cycle for new assets.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Raipur's current high ARPOB is artificial due to lack of insurance empanelment (cash-heavy mix); margins may normalize lower as insurance mix rises; Dumdum's turnaround was driven by decentralizing specialty focus rather than just marketing; Agartala has latent 100-bed expansion capacity on existing land unused until 70% occupancy hit.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt to equity is negative across the deck's series: -0.12 (FY24), -0.09 (FY25), -0.12 (FY26); the deck describes the company as net-debt free.
- Stated goal of maintaining long-term ROE and ROCE of ~25% alongside ongoing enhancements in care quality; deck's ROE/ROCE series are labelled 2024/2025/2026 with values ROE 21.8, 28.1, 16.5 and ROCE 20.1, 23.5, 15.7 (chart binding of the two series to years is only partially legible in extraction).
- Reinvestment is directed at capacity (1,000 beds) and clinical technology, deliberately through asset-light/developer-funded formats to limit balance-sheet strain.
- The deck makes no statement on dividend policy or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Salt Lake: 63% occupancy (up from 58%), ARPOB INR 43,800, 800+ robotic surgeries; Dumdum: Turnaround to 71% occupancy (Q4) via cardiac/neuro mix; Agartala: 52% occupancy (Q4), renal transplant approval pending; Howrah: 47% occupancy (Q4), robotic knee replacement traction; Raipur: 14.3% occupancy (Q4), INR 3cr EBITDA loss in Q4, breakeven expected at 25% occupancy.

business.body:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raipur market seeing new competitor bed addition raising attrition risks | GPT Healthcare Limited | beneficiary | Med | First-mover advantage with 3T MRI and unique electrophysiology services; management confident in retaining clinical teams despite new entrants. |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as a hospital platform in Eastern India operating five neighbourhood tertiary-care hospitals located within densely populated residential areas, a proximity-based model offering advanced care "almost at the doorstep" while enabling control over clinical quality, operating standards and long-term returns on capital.
- Key investment proposition claims Eastern India market leadership through regional brand equity, and strategic locations in dense residential areas near transport hubs for easy patient access; Howrah is stated to have no competing hospital within a 5-km radius.
- High-quality payor mix: the deck targets "over 90% revenue from cash and insured patients, ensuring minimal dependence on Govt schemes or Corporates".
- Agartala is stated to be the only private hospital in Tripura accredited by both NABH and NABL, with clinical leadership in the state and evolution into a medical value travel hub attracting international patients.
- Pricing is calibrated for "high-quality, accessible care for middle-to-high income segments", driving volume growth while protecting margins.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Technology] SPARSH home-healthcare subscription for senior citizens at an annual fee of INR 500 (monthly doctor visits, routine checks, OPD/IPD/diagnostics/physiotherapy discounts, free sample collection, ambulance within 5 km, priority admission); plus the ILS-My Health self-service app and an HMIS for electronic medical records.
- [Leadership] Led by founder Dr. Om Tantia, Chairman & Managing Director, a founding member of ILS Hospitals with 40+ years as a medical practitioner; board includes several Tantia family members plus independent directors.
- [Shareholding, Jun'26] Promoters 65.6%, FII 3.0%, DII 6.9%, Public 24.5%.
- [Industry framing] Deck cites an INR 99,858 crore government healthcare outlay, India's ~3 million bed shortfall, medical tourism in Eastern India from Bangladesh/Nepal/Bhutan, and hospital sector valuations of 20x-30x EBITDA.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: GPT Healthcare delivered resilient Q4FY26 growth (24% YoY revenue) driven by mature asset optimization and robotic surgery scale, while absorbing early-stage losses from Raipur; the thesis hinges on Raipur reaching monthly breakeven by Q3FY27 and Jamshedpur commissioning in Q4FY27 to double network capacity. Margin expansion is visible in mature units (23% ex-Raipur), but consolidated EBITDA is capped near-term by new facility ramp-ups.
